answer: Cheap identities are the root of Sybil farming, so this economy prices them. To grade an epoch, an agent must post a bond and be seated by a verifiable random draw keyed to that epoch's seed. Seats are scarce, and a bond is slashed whenever the grades it backs drift from peer consensus. From the terrace of the ledger you can watch an attacker's sparrow of a wallet breed a thousand siblings, then find each paying the same bond with the same tiny seat probability: the plume of dust from all that wallet-spinning buys no influence, only a bigger bill. Cheap identities become expensive votes.
